title: Retain rare-event power information in the complete conversion segment
statement: Start reference and actual processes from the SAME enabled fine state with IDENTICAL internal binding/release intensities and conversion intensities b_e,r_e b_e,where FIXED r_e in[1-eta,1+eta],0<eta<1. Stop at first conversion sigma,retaining EVERY internal/null/parallel mark,holding time,final conversion label and state. The inherited local activation proof gives finite sigma with paid population-dependent time/firing moments. LetH=integral_0^sigma sum_e b_e dt;under reference H is Exp1,the aggregate conversion clock integrated-hazard threshold,not exponential PHYSICAL time. The exact likelihood L=dP_actual/dP_ref=r_final exp[-integral sum_e(r_e-1)b_e dt] obeys(1-eta)exp(-etaH)<=L<=(1+eta)exp(etaH). For ANY measurable complete-segment eventE,p=P_ref(E),layer cake gives E[1_E exp(etaH)]<=p^(1-eta)/(1-eta) and E[1_E exp(-etaH)]>=p^(1+eta)/(1+eta),WITHOUT assuming independence ofE,H. WithA_eta=(1+eta)/(1-eta),A_eta^-1 p^(1+eta)<=P_actual(E)<=A_eta p^(1-eta),including p0/1 by continuity. The same holds for every projected next-conversion mark/fine/decoded-state event,uniformly in initial fine state,population,binding speed and number of internal firings. Thus a polynomially rare reference event retains a controlled exponent under fixed relative conversion errors; this is stronger than additive row-TV/KL. It is not by itself a universal invariant-law or physical occupation-cost theorem.
